rationale: Iter-5 changed the picture decisively. C1 now passes its intended mechanistic gate cleanly, C2 shows the core practical objective was achieved (HarmBench ASR 0.000 with near-base MT-Bench and threshold-level MMLU preservation), and C4 is substantively preserved with no agent regression and perfect BFCL. The remaining failed plan gates are not meaningful scientific negatives but floor-effects from infeasible absolute margins against baselines already at or near zero. Given only one iteration remains, the highest-value decision is to stop rather than spend it on C3, which is a distinct transfer claim requiring a fresh Mistral refit plus attack loop and may still end inconclusive within budget. I would not choose C because the evidence already supports a positive verdict without procedural re-auditing; re-audit may tidy bookkeeping but is unlikely to change the substantive conclusion. Thus the pipeline is ready in the sense requested: C1/C2/C4 are supported, while C3 should be explicitly documented as open future work rather than a blocker for this round.
